description: We are a team of students and technology enthusiasts interested in space science, technology, coding, and innovation. We are passionate about learning, researching, and developing creative solutions to real-world challenges. Our interests include Artificial Intelligence, Machine Learning, Robotics, Data Analysis, and Space Exploration. We are looking for enthusiastic team members who are interested in research, programming, problem-solving, design, and teamwork.
summary: “Dancing with the STARs,” is an interactive space animation developed using PictoBlox Block Coding. We created a virtual night sky featuring four sprites: a Dancing Star, Polaris (the North Star), a Star Group and Earth. The Dancing Star changes costumes, bounces up and down, rotates and changes colours while playing music. Polaris twinkles by continuously changing its brightness. The Star Group rotates around the centre, and Earth spins continuously to represent its rotation. Through these animations, our project demonstrates why stars appear to move across the night sky while Polaris remains almost stationary. It addresses the challenge of understanding the apparent movement of stars by transforming an astronomy concept into a fun visual coding experience. This project encourages creativity, computational thinking and scientific curiosity while helping students understand Earth's rotation and explore the wonders of space.
details:
Dancing with the STARs

Dancing with the STARs is an interactive space-themed animation developed using PictoBlox Block Coding. Our project demonstrates how stars appear to dance and move across the night sky because of Earth's rotation.

How Does Our Project Work?

We created a virtual night sky with four main sprites:

  1. Dancing Star: The star plays music, changes its costumes, rotates, moves up and down, and changes colours continuously, creating a dancing effect.
  2. Polaris (North Star): This sprite twinkles by continuously increasing and decreasing its brightness. It represents the North Star, which appears almost stationary in the sky.
  3. Star Group: A group of small stars rotates continuously around the centre, demonstrating the apparent circular movement of stars around Polaris.
  4. Earth: The Earth sprite rotates continuously to represent Earth's rotation.

We also planned interactive explanations using speech and a quiz to help users understand the science behind the animation.

Benefits and Intended Impact

  • Makes astronomy easy and interesting to understand.
  • Explains Earth's rotation through visual animation.
  • Helps students understand why stars appear to move.
  • Develops creativity, logical thinking and computational skills.
  • Encourages students to explore space science through coding.

Tools and Technologies Used

  • Software: PictoBlox
  • Programming Language: Visual Block-Based Coding
  • Coding Concepts: Events, loops, motion, costumes, sound and visual effects.
  • Sprites: Star, Polaris, Star Group and Earth.
  • Platform: Computer-based simulation.

No external hardware was required because the entire project was developed as a software-based simulation.

What Makes Our Project Creative?

Our creativity lies in combining astronomy with animation and coding. Instead of simply explaining Earth's rotation through text, we created a virtual night sky where stars twinkle, rotate and dance with music. The combination of animated characters, sound and scientific explanations makes the learning experience more engaging and interactive.

Factors Considered by Our Team

  • Scientific accuracy of the concept.
  • Correct representation of Polaris and Earth's rotation.
  • Smooth animation and sprite movements.
  • Suitable background, colours and sound effects.
  • Simple explanations that students can easily understand.
  • An engaging and educational user experience.

Our main goal is to combine science, imagination and technology to make learning about the universe fun and meaningful.
